title: Recording: Photograph, Step Lightly by Ringo Starr | 1973
content:
Sunset Sound Recorders, Los Angeles
Producer: Richard Perry
Engineer: Bill Schnee

The fifth recording session for Ringo Starr’s third studio album, Ringo, took place on 9 March 1973.

He worked on two new songs: ‘Photograph’ and ‘Step Lightly’.

‘Photograph’ had originally been recorded in late 1972 during sessions for Harrison’s fourth solo album Living In The Material World. The re-recording was begun on this day, and completed on 29 June with additional overdubs at Burbank Studios.

‘Step Lightly’ was the only song on the Ringo album to be solely credited to Starr, although he received co-writing credits on several others. It was given a cabaret-style production, in keeping with the revue-style presentation of the album.

Starr’s tap dancing can be heard from 1:40, and may have been added at Apple Studios at an unspecified date. The back cover of the album noted “the dancing feet of Richard Starkey, M.B.E.”

Ringo came in with a set of tap shoes and we overdubbed him dancing. I wish we had all the sessions on film, but that one in particular was a blast and would be the most entertaining to watch.
Bill Schnee
Chairman At The Board: Recording The Soundtrack Of A Generation
Without any lawyers knowing anything about it, we came back to LA, and in five days had recorded five tracks, which included the three major singles from the album, ‘Photograph’, ‘You’re Sixteen’ and ‘Oh My My’.
Richard Perry
The Record Producers, John Tobler and Stuart Grundy

‘Step Lightly’ was completed on 10 July 1973.
